milestones.description: Uses position_near_with_facing because this is a find/locate task. Gravel path is at (2-3, -1, 2-5) relative to spawn. Target center is (2,0,3), which is 3.6 blocks from spawn origin. Max_distance=3 requires the player to intentionally move toward the gravel (cannot be satisfied from spawn at distance 3.6). Facing_tolerance=45 ensures player is looking at the gravel path.

Uses position_near_with_facing because this is a find/locate task. Black concrete powder is at (-2,-1,1) and (-3,-1,2) relative to spawn. Target is (-2,0,1), distance from spawn is ~2.2 blocks. Max_distance=4 is generous enough to allow approach from multiple angles while still requiring the player to face the correct direction (facing_tolerance=45).

Uses position_near_with_facing because this is a find/locate task. The red nether brick crafting room front face is at z=3, with the doorway at (-5,0-1,3). Target is (-5,1,3), distance from spawn is ~5.8 blocks. Max_distance=4 requires intentional navigation to the room structure.

Uses position_near_with_facing because this is a find/locate task. Lime carpet is at (5-6, 0, 2) in front of the anvil room entrance. Target is (6,0,2), distance from spawn is ~6.3 blocks. Max_distance=4 requires intentional eastward navigation.

Uses inventory_has because mining the trapped chest causes its contents to drop as items that the player collects. The chest contains cobblestone which is NOT available anywhere else in the scene (floor is stone_bricks, walls are red_nether_bricks/stone_bricks). Having cobblestone in inventory uniquely proves the trapped chest was broken and looted.

Uses inventory_has because mining a red bed drops it as a single red_bed item into the player's inventory. The red bed blocks the crafting room doorway at (-5,0,3-4). No other red beds exist in the scene, so possession uniquely proves this bed was mined.

Uses inventory_has with min_count=2 because TWO stacked brick stairs block the anvil room doorway at (6,0,3) and (6,1,3). The player is 1.8 blocks tall, so both must be mined to create a passable 2-high opening. Each stair drops 1 brick_stairs item. No other brick_stairs exist in the scene.

Uses inventory_has because crafting cobblestone_slab (3 cobblestone in a row at crafting table) produces slabs that appear in the player's inventory. Cobblestone_slab is not placed anywhere in the scene and is only obtainable through crafting, making this a unique verification of the craft action.

Uses inventory_has because crafting an oak_fence_gate (2 oak_planks + 4 sticks in stick-plank-stick pattern on two rows) produces the gate item in inventory. Oak_fence_gate is not available anywhere else in the scene and is only obtainable through crafting.

Uses inventory_has because the shield is ONLY accessible inside the anvil room chest (behind the brick stairs barrier). Having shield in inventory proves the player: (1) mined both brick stairs to clear the doorway, (2) entered the anvil room, (3) opened the equipment chest. While this cannot verify the actual rename action at the anvil, it confirms the player completed all physical prerequisites and obtained the item from its gated location. KNOWN LIMITATION: Cannot verify custom name was applied.

Uses inventory_has because the iron_chestplate is ONLY accessible inside the anvil room chest (behind the brick stairs barrier). Same reasoning as rename_shield - possession proves barrier was cleared and anvil room was accessed. KNOWN LIMITATION: Cannot verify custom name was applied.

Uses inventory_has because cooked_salmon is ONLY accessible inside the crafting room chest (behind the red bed barrier). Having cooked_salmon in inventory proves the player: (1) mined the red bed to clear the doorway, (2) entered the crafting room, (3) opened the salmon chest. The chest contains 2 salmon; after eating 1, the player retains 1 (satisfying min_count=1). KNOWN LIMITATION: Verifies retrieval from gated location, not consumption itself. However, retrieval requires completing the mine_red_bed prerequisite.
